object_description: independent new hall building in the second row behind the retained historic gymnasium
geometry_property: geometric cut-outs in the plinth cladding
design_condition: the historic gymnasium is retained and the new hall placed behind it on the south side as an independent building, so that with the existing barn the ensemble forms a forum-like village square

positive: The existing building is recognised as a defining element and retained as a place of collective memory
Preserving it actively counteracts the fraying of the village
The existing building appears unchanged as a solitaire and is only carefully converted inside
All main uses are on the ground floor and open to the open spaces on all sides
Together with the existing barn the ensemble forms a forum-like village square with a strong identity
The new building integrates surprisingly unobtrusively into the complex despite its impressive volume
The overhanging pitched roof and wooden materials use familiar yet pleasantly restrained means
The ground plan and facades are skilfully structured by the timber construction
The dark rear-ventilated facade and the refined plinth cladding lend the extension sophistication
The chosen concepts relate to the overall complex and are solid and durable
The ground-level double gymnasium enables excellent connections and permeability to the open spaces
Two multi-purpose rooms beside the foyer can also be used as an extension of it
The second access point by the stage guarantees access to both halls when in use
The existing hall is renovated and redesigned with minimal intervention
The principles of the existing site are consistently developed and the existing qualities strengthened
The mature trees are largely preserved
The access situation and the garage entrance position are clearly laid out
The forum-like open space between the three buildings is attractively designed with high utility value
The stage area can be opened to the east for open-air uses
The hall can be built independently of school operations, avoiding costly temporary arrangements
The structure is designed to be durable and resource-efficient
A fully integrated photovoltaic system and well-insulated envelope promise an attractive energy concept
The efficient room layout and construction concepts make the new building highly cost-effective
negative: The staircase prevents the interesting synergy of the upper multi-purpose room as a gallery to the hall
The main stage lacks side stages or the required multi-purpose rooms at the same level
Equipment storage split over several rooms, some upstairs with lift access, is not feasible as proposed
This is an unacceptable deficit for daily operation of the gyms
The checkrooms for festivities sit next to the very small foyer
Access to both halls is not barrier-free
Users prefer a fixed room allocation for the playgroup
The kitchen on the mezzanine of the old building is unsuitable for catering events in the new hall
Including the existing barn offers no advantages for client and school
The numerous storage areas are an oversupply of space detrimental to economic viability
The number of parking spaces is clearly too small
The all-weather pitch takes a considerable part of the heavily used playing field
Additional costs arise for renovation, the extra mini hall and preserving the barn
The multi-purpose hall does not meet the requirements for daily school operation or for hosting events
